A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same NPR research. The complete text, equations, figures and tables are readable, including v3 Appendices A–D. Relocated material can be reliably matched.

before.justification: V1 reports original NPR training and benchmark results, throughput measurements, parallel-trigger rates, learning dynamics and generated case studies.

after.justification: V3 retains these original empirical results, including the test-time scalability results and case studies relocated to Appendices C and D.

M1.justification: The three-stage training pipeline, parallel attention and positions, PAPO objective and NPR Engine procedures remain unchanged. Algorithms 1–2 move to Appendix A; removing descriptions of unsuccessful preliminary approaches does not change the final method.

E1.justification: Both use ORZ training data and evaluate AIME24, AIME25, HMMT25, OlympiadBench, Minerva-Math, ZebraLogic, AMC23 and MATH500. The appendices introduce no additional dataset or task coverage.

E2.justification: The corresponding benchmark comparisons retain Qwen2.5-32B-Instruct, both Qwen3-4B variants, Multiverse-32B/4B and SR/SR-BETA. Comparator membership in the throughput, trigger-rate and scalability comparisons also remains unchanged.

E3.justification: Removing v1 Section 4.6 removes exploratory configurations involving Qwen2.5-7B/base models and alternative thinking-block training procedures. The retained experiments keep the same ORZ-8k subset, generation limits, learning rates and avg@8/avg@1/best@8 evaluation settings.

E4.justification: V3 omits Section 4.6's exploratory failure analyses, including thinking-model training attempts and comparisons of original versus unfolded Multiverse branches. The principal efficiency, trigger-rate, learning-dynamics and scalability analyses and both case studies remain.

E5.justification: Neither version reports statistical replication counts, random seeds, confidence intervals or significance tests. The same sampled-answer counts and avg@k/best@8 reporting practices are retained.

E6.justification: Tables 2–5 retain identical numerical results, including NPR's 50.4 AIME25 score and 4.6× speedup. V3 removes qualitative findings from Section 4.6 about token fragmentation, unstable masked-thinking training, nearly identical branch-SFT outcomes and unsuccessful weaker-backbone training.

T1.justification: The dependency factorization, rejection-sampling rule and policy objectives are unchanged, with no added theory or proofs. Equation 4 consistently marks generated answers with hats in v3; this corrects notation without changing the mathematical procedure.

C1.justification: The central teacher-free NPR, PAPO and engine contributions and headline performance claims remain. Removing Section 1.1 also drops its explicit capability claim about distinct strategies for creative versus logical tasks, modestly narrowing the stated claim scope.

C2.justification: V3 removes the hypothesis that modifying thinking blocks disrupts RL priors and the explanation that weak instruction following and reasoning undermine Stage-1 training on weaker backbones. The general warning about thinking-mode SFT and the retained case-study failure discussion remain.

D1.justification: V1's explicit code, model and project-website links disappear from v3. Main training hyperparameters, engine details and pseudocode remain available in the document. The PDFs establish removal of access information, not withdrawal of the resources themselves.

R1.justification: The cited works and central positioning relative to earlier parallel-reasoning and RL methods remain unchanged. Related Work moves from Section 5 to Appendix B; bibliography ordering, styling and citation-year suffix changes do not introduce different works.

P1.justification: V3 substantially reorganizes the document: algorithms, related work, scalability and case studies become Appendices A–D; the Contributions and Preliminary Exploration sections disappear; and an Impact Statement is added. Most retained scientific prose remains substantially unchanged.

P2.justification: The single-column report becomes a two-column conference layout with single-column appendices. Figures 2–4 shrink to column width, Figure 1 moves, and algorithms and Tables 5–7 relocate. All figures and tables remain; Table 5 has clearer column spacing.

improvement.justification: Reduced repetition and clearer Table 5 spacing provide presentation benefits. However, v3 removes informative failed explorations and backbone limitations from Section 4.6, together with direct code/model access links. With the principal methods and results unchanged, these omissions modestly reduce transparency and reproducibility guidance.
